chapter: Decca years and the First Herd
title: Decca contract, Roseland and the Famous Door: struggling to survive
summary: The band was nearly a Decca house band, covering hits, and survived the early lean years at Roseland, on the road and at the Famous Door.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: You continued the contract with Decca Records then that Isham had had when he left.

Well, it was a new contract and a whole new thing -- yeah, same company, however, yeah. No, we actually played for the people at Decca, the Kapp Brothers, and then we became almost like a house band there the first couple or three years. That was about the only thing that kept us
together, because work was very -- well, we had a job right from the beginning, Roseland, which didn't pay very well. But we managed to stay there for a lot of months.

And then, when we went out to go on the road because we'd had some air time, along with a few records released, we couldn't be booked very well. And so consequently, for a year or two it was a real battle to stay alive, to make it work. And if we hadn't had Decca going, we probably would have collapsed completely. But eventually we got a couple of records that got some play and eventually went back to New York, after hanging out in New England along with a lot of other bands, trying to eke out an existence.
Went back to New York and opened a place called The Famous Door on 52nd Street, and then things started to perk up a little.
Well, you did numerous records, a whole long string, for --
Well, we were almost like a house band at that -- yeah.
As I recall, even in some of the tunes, reflected the policy of that day, that everyone was trying to cover a tune.
Yeah, that's right. If there was a hit on Victor, then Decca -- we'd be in to do it the next week.
You had a lot of vocals.
And you had a small group, too.

Well, they allowed us to do that so we could get involved in the jazz thing, which we were all interested in. And they knew that that's what I wanted to do, so they allowed me to do that. But that took a while, that didn't happen right from the beginning.
In other words, do two for them and I might get to do one later.
Uh-huh. Were you -- you had a good group of competent people in your band.
Oh, yes, and we were constantly trying to improve it, and getting better writing and better everything.
